title: Chicken and Cashew Stir Fry
description: A light stir fry carried by three sauces and a handful of toasted cashews. Grill the cashews with one eye on them, because they go from golden to burnt in under a minute.
equipment: wok or large non-stick frying pan

items.raw: 500 g skinless chicken breast fillets, sliced

items.note: cut in half lengthways then thinly sliced
items.raw: 1/2 cup carrots cut half length ways then thinly sliced

steps.text: Spread the cashews on a baking tray and grill until browned. Watch them, because they go from golden to burnt in well under a minute. Set aside.
Coat a wok or large non-stick frying pan with cooking spray and saute the garlic and chicken together until the chicken is cooked. Lift the chicken into a bowl and set aside.
Add the onion, chilli, capsicums, snow peas and carrots to the pan and stir for 3 to 5 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pan.
Blend the cornflour with the water and pour it into the pan with the stock powder, fish sauce, oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, pepper and shallots, stirring well.
Once the sauce has thickened, serve with boiled rice or noodles and scatter the cashews over each serve.

notes: The source offers 500 g lean beef strips, 500 g green prawns or 400 g tofu in place of the chicken.
Leaving the cashews out drops the fat by 3.7 g a serve, but they are most of the reason to make it.
The three sauces plus the stock powder do the seasoning, so it needs no added salt. Sodium is still around 790 mg a serve.

nutrition.assumptions: Energy, fat, fibre, protein and carbohydrate are read off the printed panel, chicken column. The panel gives no saturated fat, sugars or sodium, so those three are estimated from the ingredients: saturated fat mostly from the cashews and chicken, sodium almost entirely from the fish, oyster and soy sauces plus the stock powder. Serving size of 290 g is worked out from the ingredient masses, roughly 1.3 kg reducing about 10% over four servings, and the per-100 g column is derived from that.
